sourcedFrom: PALMETTO 5.7 ROCK® USER’S MANUAL — P45-0004-00 — part number printed on the back page (not printed in the book — the part number P45-0004-00 is its only edition mark)
cleanIntro: The 5.7 Rock is a striker-fired 5.7x28 pistol, and its takedown asks for a pulled trigger on an empty gun and a slide held back only about 1/4 inch while the takedown lever comes down. Hold it further back than that and the trigger resets, which sends you back to the start. The book stops at the field strip — slide, recoil spring assembly and barrel — and it asks for very little oil.

steps.title: Magazine out
steps.action: Point the muzzle in a safe direction with your finger off the trigger. Press the magazine catch button on the grip and pull the magazine free.
steps.prose: This pistol has no magazine disconnect, so taking the magazine out proves nothing about the chamber.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine by depressing the magazine catch button found on the grip
steps.cite: PALMETTO 5.7 ROCK® USER’S MANUAL — P45-0004-00 — part number printed on the back page — Firearm Safety — unloading, printed p.18

steps.title: Slide fully back and lock it open
steps.action: Hold the grip firmly with your firing hand and grip the rear of the slide with your support hand. Pull the slide all the way back and push the slide stop lever up, then let the slide come forward onto the lever. Any round in the chamber ejects on the way back.
steps.prose: Let the slide come forward under control onto the slide stop rather than riding it — you want it parked open, not closed on a round.
steps.quote: Pull the slide to the full rearward position and manually push the slide stop lever up
steps.cite: PALMETTO 5.7 ROCK® USER’S MANUAL — P45-0004-00 — part number printed on the back page — Firearm Safety — unloading, printed p.18

steps.title: ⛔ Look AND feel — the chamber must be empty
steps.action: With the slide held open, look into the chamber and then put a fingertip in it. Only an empty chamber you have both seen and felt counts as clear.
steps.prose: The next step on this pistol is a trigger pull, and that is exactly when a chamber you only glanced at will matter.
steps.caution: A cartridge in the chamber will discharge if the trigger is pulled, even in the absence of an inserted magazine.
steps.quote: There may still be a cartridge in the chamber even when the magazine is removed.
steps.cite: PALMETTO 5.7 ROCK® USER’S MANUAL — P45-0004-00 — part number printed on the back page — Firearm Safety — unloading, printed p.18

steps.title: ⛔ Trigger pulled on the EMPTY gun
steps.action: Release the slide so it closes on the empty chamber. With the pistol empty and the muzzle somewhere safe, pull the trigger fully to the rear. The takedown that follows starts from this fired condition.
steps.prose: If you are about to pull the trigger without having just seen and felt an empty chamber, stop and check again.
steps.quote: With the firearm empty and pointed in a safe direction, fully pull the trigger rearward.
steps.cite: PALMETTO 5.7 ROCK® USER’S MANUAL — P45-0004-00 — part number printed on the back page — Disassembly, printed p.27

steps.title: Slide back about 1/4 inch — and hold it there
steps.action: Wrap your firing hand around the pistol and squeeze thumb and fingers together while your index finger presses the slide rearward. Stop when about 1/4 inch of the slide hangs over the back of the frame, and hold it there.
steps.prose: Overshooting is the mistake this step invites: pull it much past 1/4 inch and the trigger resets, and the takedown has to start again from the trigger pull.
steps.caution: Do not allow it to move much more than this distance rearward, as it will reset the trigger
steps.quote: Allow it to travel rearward until approximately 1/4” of the slide hangs over the rear of the frame.
steps.cite: PALMETTO 5.7 ROCK® USER’S MANUAL — P45-0004-00 — part number printed on the back page — Disassembly, printed p.27

steps.title: Takedown lever down on both sides
steps.action: Still holding the slide back, use your support hand to pull the takedown lever fully down — on both sides of the frame.
steps.prose: Half-down on one side is not down. If the slide will not come forward off the frame in the next step, this lever is the first thing to check.
steps.quote: pull the takedown lever fully downward on both sides
steps.cite: PALMETTO 5.7 ROCK® USER’S MANUAL — P45-0004-00 — part number printed on the back page — Disassembly, printed p.27

steps.title: Slide forward and lift it off
steps.action: Ease off the pressure with your firing hand and let the slide run forward until the grip sticks out about 3/8 inch past the back of the slide. Then lift the slide up off the frame.
steps.prose: The slide comes off upward at this point, not forward off the end of the rails.
steps.quote: allowing the slide to move forward until the grip overhangs the slide approximately 3/8”. You can then lift the slide up off of the frame.
steps.cite: PALMETTO 5.7 ROCK® USER’S MANUAL — P45-0004-00 — part number printed on the back page — Disassembly, printed p.27

steps.title: Recoil spring assembly out
steps.action: With the slide in hand, press the rear of the recoil spring assembly toward the muzzle about 1/8 inch, rotate it upward to clear the lugs under the barrel, then let the pressure off and lift the whole assembly out of the slide.
steps.prose: It is under spring pressure while you rotate it, so keep control of the rear until it is clear of the lugs.
steps.quote: pressing the rear of the assembly toward the muzzle roughly 1/8” then rotating it upward to clear the lugs on the bottom of the barrel.
steps.cite: PALMETTO 5.7 ROCK® USER’S MANUAL — P45-0004-00 — part number printed on the back page — Disassembly, printed p.28

steps.title: Barrel out along its bore axis
steps.action: Turn the slide upside down. Grip the barrel by the locking lugs on its underside, lift and draw it rearward, and keep lifting the rear while sliding it back and up along its own bore line until it clears the slide.
steps.prose: Follow the bore's own line out — levering it sideways only binds it in the slide.
steps.quote: Continue to lift the rear while also sliding the barrel rearward and upward along its current bore axis until it is clear of the slide
steps.cite: PALMETTO 5.7 ROCK® USER’S MANUAL — P45-0004-00 — part number printed on the back page — Disassembly, printed p.28

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Four groups on the bench: frame, slide, recoil spring assembly and barrel. That is as far as Palmetto takes this pistol apart, and as far as this guide goes.
steps.prose: The manual forbids taking the pistol apart beyond what it outlines, so the striker, extractor and fire-control parts stay where they are.
steps.quote: The pistol is now in the “field stripped” condition
steps.cite: PALMETTO 5.7 ROCK® USER’S MANUAL — P45-0004-00 — part number printed on the back page — Disassembly, printed p.28

deepAbsentReason: The user's manual ends at the field strip (printed pp.27–28): slide, recoil spring assembly and barrel. Its cleaning and lubrication sections (pp.33–37) work on those parts only, and p.10 forbids disassembly beyond what the manual outlines.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Look down the bore from the chamber end: there must be a clear, visible path. An obstructed bore means do not fire the pistol again and call Palmetto State Armory.
Lightly lubricate the outside of the barrel — the lugs, the lockup surface and the areas that contact the slide.

cleaning.name: SLIDE
tasks: Clean the breech face, the extractor claw and the slide rails.
⚠ Keep the fouling and excess cleaner away from the striker area — residue there can impair the trigger pull or cause failures to fire.
Wipe the slide down and inspect it for cleanliness.
Lightly lubricate the inside of the slide where it contacts the barrel, and inside the rail slots.

cleaning.name: FRAME
tasks: Nylon brush and cleaner-lubricant inside the frame: the slide rails, the locking cam, and the fire-control and sear.
Wipe the frame down and inspect it for cleanliness.
Lightly lubricate the rails, the sear and the disconnector.

cleaning.name: RECOIL SPRING ASSEMBLY
tasks: Nylon brush and cleaner-lubricant on the recoil spring.
Wipe it down and inspect it for cleanliness.
Do not over-oil anything: this pistol needs only a minimal amount of lubricant, and too much collects debris and causes malfunctions.

reassembly: Barrel into the slide: slide upside down, barrel lugs up. Feed the muzzle through the hole at the front of the slide until about 1/8 inch shows, lower the chamber end in, then slide the barrel back until its breech meets the slide.

Recoil spring assembly: front end into the smaller hole at the front of the slide. Press the rear forward to compress the plunger and rod until it clears the barrel lugs, rotate it down until it seats on the flat at the front of the barrel lug, then let it lock rearward against the lug.

Slide onto the frame: finger off the trigger and outside the guard. Line the slide's rail pockets up with the frame rails, push the slide down to seat it, then pull it rearward as if cycling — listen for the click of the takedown lever re-engaging — and on to the full end of its travel.
Function check the pistol before you fire it.
fncheck: Clear the pistol first, by sight and by feel. Palmetto's function check for the 5.7 Rock is printed as a sequence of pictures on pages 31–32 of the user's manual — work through it before the pistol is fired, and clear the pistol again when you finish.
